You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: Assess the same jacket's front closure in SOURCE and EDITED, distinguishing visible evidence of progress from evidence of the complete endpoint. Full achievement requires the front panels to meet along the closure with no visible opening. Concrete, reliably visible movement of the panels toward one another may establish partial fulfillment even if the entire closure cannot be seen. Do not infer progress from a change in pose or jacket motion alone. If neither progress nor completion can be judged from visible evidence, fulfillment is unobservable and must remain unresolved, not be scored as zero.
node.binding: Compare the woman's jacket in SOURCE with that same jacket in EDITED. Assess the same front-closure region where it is visible, accounting for pose, occlusion, and visibility. Judge concrete visible movement of the panels toward one another as partial closure, and a visibly joined closure with no opening as complete. Assign no progress only when the same region is reliably comparable and shows no movement toward closure or is more open. Do not treat turning, swinging, or flaring of the jacket by itself as evidence that the panels moved together. If neither progress nor completion can be judged from visible evidence, preserve uncertainty rather than assigning zero or inferring progress.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The same closure region is reliably visible and comparable in SOURCE and EDITED, and shows no movement of the front panels toward one another or shows that the jacket is more open. Pose change or jacket motion alone is not evidence of progress. If neither progress nor completion can be judged because the relevant evidence is obscured, leave fulfillment unresolved.
node.half_when: Visible, reliable evidence shows the front panels moving partway toward one another, but a visible opening remains; score the concrete incomplete closure as partial fulfillment. Do not infer this from pose change or jacket motion alone. If neither progress nor completion can be judged, preserve uncertainty as an unknown interval rather than assigning a score.
node.full_when: The front panels visibly meet along the jacket closure with no visible opening remaining, as established from the visible closure region despite any pose change.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket is open in SOURCE, with a visible gap between the front panels. In EDITED, the woman has turned and the jacket flares outward; the front closure is not clearly visible, and there is no reliable evidence that the panels moved toward one another or met. The apparent change is jacket motion/pose, not demonstrated closure progress.
